policy: Source-derived assertion responsibilities, not an implementation capability list. Every required statement remains pending until exact evidence exists. Mixed files retain shared effects and explicitly exclude only tty observations.

required: Text versus argv grammar; source-order bare/hidden assignments; inactive branches; prepare-before-execute; includes, aliases, source paths and diagnostics.
Configuration executes once across starter disconnects; queued commands and callbacks cannot access freed clients; waiting clients observe completion.
Global/session environment inheritance, cleared versus hidden versus removed values, update-environment globs on attach, shell escaping, errors, child environment and default command/shell.
Names, IDs, exact/prefix/glob/ambiguous targets, offsets, directional and marked targets, session groups, linked windows, insertion/renumber limits and current/last state.
All applicable command flags, filtering/format contexts, errors and atomic failure effects; attach/switch/detach affect control/native views.
outside: Ordinary tty attach redraw is excluded; ordinary tty attachment must be rejected by the IPC adapter.

required: Split/break/join/move/swap/rotate/resize/select geometry, tiled/custom layouts and nesting limits, zoom restoration, floating/modal ownership and rejection rollback.
Border footprint affects C command geometry even though native views paint borders; preserve grid coordinates and process resize effects.
outside: Floating border glyphs, full-screen repaint bytes and status painting are presentation only.

required: Real process spawn, empty panes, respawn replacement and exit status, wait-for-process completion, child/descendant cleanup and client-loss callback safety.
Ending a session or respawning a window preserves remaining active IDs and releases dead process/output references.
outside: Attached tty redraw after respawn is excluded; native snapshots still report the new active pane and unzoomed layout.

required: Queued shell/conditional jobs, target cwd, command stdout/status, nested command ordering, hooks and waits, callback lifetime after client loss and hooks on graph/process/input state.
Hook flags and array insertion/removal preserve command order and source context; wait cancellation frees the queue.
outside: TTY-only mode/status/prompt hooks cannot fire when that presentation is unavailable; native UI actions need explicit adapter policy.

required: Named/automatic paste buffers, binary bytes, append/rename/eviction/filtering, load/save stdout and file errors, paste separators/raw/bracketed/delete behavior, clipboard policy and pipe-pane process lifetime.
All in-profile options enforce types/ranges, scopes and inheritance, array indices/keys/append/unset/quiet semantics, abbreviations and errors; user options remain extensible.
Presentation-only options listed separately must reject unsupported changes explicitly; accepting an inert setting is not evidence of support.

Control command guards, notifications/subscriptions/layout variants, client sizing/flags, guarded output, bounded exit and stalled-client behavior, client identification failures and late job completion.
Preserve exact record bytes and causal order; new protocol flags and notifications require version/capability review.

Socket endpoint identity/private access, path validation, startup failures, read-only command restrictions, ACL policy and explicit diagnostics; late resize/exit messages cannot access a closed client.

list-commands exposes the complete C command metadata and aliases/usage; explicit capability support and unsupported execution policy are separate. Command diagnostics and structured output preserve bytes.
outside: Cross-UID server-access may be explicitly unsupported under same-user-only policy, but must reject rather than silently widen access.

required: Application escape/OSC input, main/alternate/history screens, saved cursor/modes/margins/tabs, Unicode widths/reflow/padding, SGR/capture ranges and raw state, malformed/incomplete sequence handling and bounded parsers.
Terminal replies are emitted once by the owner; OSC titles/path/progress/shell markers, palette/theme and clipboard behavior survive detached operation.
Capture flags and escaping are command contracts, independently of whether ordinary tty rendering exists.
Literal/named/control/extended keys, paste and focus/mouse encoding to children, synchronized panes and target routing use application modes; native key events do not require a raw tty key parser.
send-prefix sends the configured prefix to children. send-keys -K and key-table dispatch require a native adapter or explicit unsupported error.
outside: Raw physical-terminal escape timing/prefix tables and terminfo input decoding are not the native adapter input path.

required: Context fields, nested conditionals/short-circuit booleans, comparisons/glob/regex/fuzzy matching, quoting/path/width/padding/trim/repeat, arithmetic and limits, substitution, time, loops, name/content lookup and source errors.
Disable jobs in config conditions; runtime format jobs require explicit effects and bounded completion. Unknown required modifiers do not count as conformant when rejected.
Style-aware width/trim returns the same format bytes even without a tty renderer; format fields are split by observable context below.
outside: Animation timer redraws, style painting and client status layout are excluded; A expansion outside a status context still follows C semantics.

required: SIXEL/Kitty decoding, replies, upload/placement IDs, layers/crops/scroll/grid operations, clearing/deletion, alternate/main ownership, history, resize recovery, resource quotas and persistence.
Native image snapshots retain the same pixels/placements/lifetimes when C tests inspect them through a rendered terminal.
outside: Client-specific SIXEL re-encoding, ASCII fallback brightness glyphs, renderer caches, erase/redraw counts and tty image frame transport are excluded.

required: View damage/snapshots preserve complete wide cells, independent clients, blocked-client recovery, viewports, synchronized output boundaries and stationary cursor visibility.
Shell output markers survive history eviction/reflow and drive native selection/search/output extraction; UI mode entry is separate from terminal data ownership.
Active pane style and reported host theme remain native-visible state.
outside: The C script tty-byte repaint and ANSI synchronization counts are excluded; port the retained-state and transaction assertions to native snapshots.

required: Chooser/prompt/menu/copy/clock/lock/binding command paths must either produce documented native effects or return an explicit unsupported error without graph, buffer, child-input or option mutation.
Control display-popup cannot block or corrupt the queue even when unsupported. Nested UI actions and mode lifetime tests become adapter/no-mutation tests, not a requirement for tmux drawn widgets.
A declared unsupported mode must also reject dependent -X/-K and UI-only command flags; native selection/search remain required in native-view-effects.
outside: Tmux chooser ordering/keys, copy-mode cursor/selection commands, prompt editing/history widgets, clock faces and lock/suspend terminal presentation are outside the engine UI profile.

Physical-terminal raw key/escape/paste/reply parsing, terminfo capability discovery and terminal reply redraw are excluded. Child key encoding is separately required by child-input; native theme/query handling by terminal-state.

Ordinary attached tty border/status/scrollbar/menu/prompt glyphs, clipping/composition and redraw/erase/cache optimizations are excluded. Shared geometry, complete cell state and native damage are separately required.
Status range hit testing and bindings target tmux-drawn UI and are excluded; native layout gestures use typed engine commands.

required: Setting any listed option must have documented native behavior or fail explicitly without mutation; storing a value that has no effect is not support.
Query defaults/absence consistently and report the unsupported profile; presentation exclusion is never a parser/validation bypass.
outside: ANSI redraw, tty title, status/menu/prompt/copy-mode decoration and dead-pane text rendering are excluded.

required: Every listed field exposes its actual graph/client/process/terminal context with C-compatible value formatting and empty values only when its context is absent.

Nondeterministic PID/time/path values use asserted relations and controlled clocks, not wholesale normalization. System-client receives remote fields as opaque bytes; it does not implement C server callbacks.

Fields whose tmux UI or physical tty context does not exist return the documented absent-context value; never invent an attached tty or copy-mode state. The buffer/client/tree mode-format callbacks return the upstream static templates even without a widget.
Native pointer/search state may expose a distinct typed API. Native/control client dimensions/theme remain required observable fields, not absent context.
outside: Populated tmux copy/chooser/status pointer/key-table callbacks are outside profile. Remote C provides them normally; control-client identification fields remain required.
